correctness.rationale: If a maximizing sequence in \(S_{\ell_p}\) were weakly null, the Bessaga-Pełczyński selection principle gives a subsequence equivalent to a normalized block basic sequence, hence to the canonical \(\ell_p\) basis. For finite \(r\ge p^*=p/(p-1)\), that basis is weakly \(r\)-summable because every dual coordinate sequence lies in \(\ell_{p^*}\subseteq\ell_r\); equivalence preserves weak \(r\)-summability. Thus a weakly \(r\)-singular maximizing sequence cannot be weakly null, so WMP forces norm attainment. The converse SMP\(_r\Rightarrow\)WMP and SMP\(_r\Rightarrow r\)-CPP are published general propositions. With an isometric \(\ell_p\) subspace in the codomain, the negative side for \(r<p^*\) follows by the published subspace inheritance and exact \((\ell_p,\ell_p)\) thresholds.

originality.rationale: The focal paper itself contains the entire transfer mechanism. Its Corollary 2.3 proves the positive \((\ell_p,L_p)\) case by exactly the same block-basis argument: a weakly \(r\)-singular maximizing sequence cannot be weakly null for \(r\ge p^*\), after which the only codomain input is that the pair has WMP. Replacing the named codomain by an arbitrary \(Y\) under the explicit hypothesis '$(\ell_p,Y)$ has WMP' is therefore a mechanical abstraction of the published proof, while Proposition 2.1, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 2.2 and Examples 4.2 already supply the converse, inheritance, perturbation implication, and sharp \((\ell_p,\ell_p)\) threshold.
